content.text: {"primary_meaning":"In mainstream Christian interpretation, milk primarily symbolizes elementary or basic spiritual teaching — the foundational nourishment appropriate to new or immature believers, typically contrasted with 'solid food' (meat), which represents mature, advanced doctrine. The image carries two related inflections: a positive one (milk as the pure, life-giving Word of God that new converts should crave) and a corrective one (remaining on milk as a sign of stunted spiritual growth).","primary_basis":["1 Corinthians 3:1-2 — Paul says he fed the Corinthians with milk, not solid food, because they were infants in Christ and not yet ready","Hebrews 5:12-14 — those needing milk are unskilled in the word of righteousness; solid food is for the mature","1 Peter 2:2 — 'like newborn infants, long for the pure spiritual milk, that by it you may grow up into salvation'","1 Corinthians 9:7 — milk as rightful nourishment from the flock (supporting the nourishment motif)"],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Abundance, blessing, and covenant prosperity — the 'land flowing with milk and honey' as a symbol of God's provision and the fertility of the Promised Land","basis":["Exodus 3:8","Exodus 3:17","Numbers 13:27","Deuteronomy 6:3","Joshua 5:6","Ezekiel 20:6"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Free grace and gospel blessings offered without cost — milk and wine bought 'without money and without price'","basis":["Isaiah 55:1"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Love, sweetness, and marital/sensual delight in Hebrew love poetry, often allegorized in Christian tradition as the sweetness of Christ's love or of Scripture","basis":["Song of Solomon 4:11","Song of Solomon 5:1","Song of Solomon 5:12"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Christ himself as the believer's nourishment — a patristic allegorical reading (notably Clement of Alexandria, Paedagogus) in which milk is the Logos who feeds the faithful","basis":["1 Peter 2:2 (read christologically, some manuscripts/interpretations linking to 'the Lord' in 2:3)","1 Corinthians 3:2 (patristic allegory)"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Purity and whiteness as a descriptive image (e.g., of health or beauty), without doctrinal symbolism","basis":["Lamentations 4:7","Genesis 49:12"],"prominence":"rare"}],"has_settled_consensus":true,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is a well-established, widely taught consensus: in the New Testament epistles, milk symbolizes elementary doctrine or basic spiritual nourishment for the spiritually immature, contrasted with solid food for the mature. Commentators routinely note the tension between the negative use in Paul and Hebrews (milk as a rebuke of immaturity) and the positive use in 1 Peter (milk as the pure Word to be craved); these are usually treated as complementary rather than contradictory. The Old Testament 'milk and honey' usage is a distinct, equally recognizable symbol of covenant abundance rather than of teaching, so context determines which sense applies."}
